1.note: This is an imperative, but it communicates an exhortation rather than a command. The psalmist is encouraging **righteous ones** to worship. If the imperative does not communicate an exhortation for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates an exhortation or invitation. Alternate translation: [You righteous ones should shout for joy in Yahweh]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **joy**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Rejoice]

The psalmist is using the adjective **righteous** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [righteous people]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **praise**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for the upright should praise him]

The psalmist is using the adjective **upright** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [for those who are upright]

2.note: The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [give thanks with a lyre of ten strings]

A **lyre of ten** is a kind of musical instrument that has ten strings stretched across it and is plucked to produce sound. If your readers would not be familiar with what a lyre is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a ten-stringed instrument]

3.note: This is an imperative, but it communicates an exhortation rather than a command. The psalmist is encouraging the people to worship. If the imperative does not communicate an exhortation for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates an exhortation or invitation. Alternate translation: [You should sing to him a new song]

4.note: Here the psalmist is speaking of Yahweh always speaking truth as if his **word** were standing straight or **upright**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For Yahweh always does what he says that he will do]
Here, **the word of Yahweh** represents what Yahweh said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh has said]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is done in a faithful way] or [is done faithfully]

5.note: The psalmist is using the possessive form to describe **Yahweh** who is characterized by **covenant faithfulness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Yahweh faithfully keeps his covenant throughout the earth]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **righteousness** and **justice**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [what is righteous and fair]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the ways Yahweh is faithful to his covenant]

Here the psalmist is speaking of the **covenant faithfulness of Yahweh** as if it were something that could **fill** the earth like water fills a container. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [extends to everyone on the earth]

The psalmist is using **the earth** to represent everyone who lives on the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [everyone on the earth]

6.q: בִּ⁠דְבַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה שָׁמַ֣יִם נַעֲשׂ֑וּ וּ⁠בְ⁠ר֥וּחַ פִּ֝֗י⁠ו כָּל־צְבָאָֽ⁠ם
6.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, connect the phrases with a word that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Another approach would be to combine them and express the emphasis in another way. See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in the Psalms, and follow that approach here and throughout this psalm. Alternate translation: [By the word of Yahweh the heavens were made, indeed, by the breath of his mouth, all of their host] or [By his command, Yahweh made the heavens and everything in them]

Here, **the word of Yahweh** represents the command that Yahweh spoke using words. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [By the command of Yahweh] or [When Yahweh commanded]

The expression **were made** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [he made the heavens]

Here, **the breath of his mouth** represents Yahweh speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and by what Yahweh spoke]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [all the stars in the heavens were made]

7.note: The point of this comparison is that just as a **heap** is a large mass piled together, so Yahweh gathered the sea waters together into a large mass. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [all piled together into one place]

Here the psalmist is speaking of the deep waters of the ocean as if they were goods that could be placed in **storehouses**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he contains the deep waters within their boundaries]

8.q: יִֽירְא֣וּ מֵ֭⁠יְהוָה כָּל־הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ מִמֶּ֥⁠נּוּ יָ֝ג֗וּרוּ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל
8.note: The psalmist is saying what he wants the people to do. See the discussion in the introduction to this book about “let” and “may” and follow the decision of your team of how a speaker will express in this context what he wants someone to do. Alternate translation: [all of the earth should fear Yahweh; all of the dwellers of the world should be in dread of him]

8.q: יִֽירְא֣וּ מֵ֭⁠יְהוָה כָּל־הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ מִמֶּ֥⁠נּוּ יָ֝ג֗וּרוּ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל
8.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [everyone in the world should fear Yahweh, indeed, they should all be in dread of him]
The psalmist is using the term **earth** to mean all the people who live on the earth. Alternate translation: [all the people of the earth]

9.q: כִּ֤י ה֣וּא אָמַ֣ר וַ⁠יֶּ֑הִי הֽוּא־צִ֝וָּ֗ה וַֽ⁠יַּעֲמֹֽד
9.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [Because when he spoke, everything he commanded came into existence]

The psalmist is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verbs translated as **he spoke** and **he commanded** already include this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it was Yahweh and no other who spoke and commanded. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [he himself spoke and it came to be; he himself commanded, and it stood]
The pronoun **it** refers to the earth. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and the earth came to be; he, he commanded, and the earth stood]

By **it stood**, the psalmist means that the earth came into existence or was created. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and it was created]

10.q: יְֽהוָ֗ה הֵפִ֥יר עֲצַת־גּוֹיִ֑ם הֵ֝נִ֗יא מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת עַמִּֽים
10.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [Yahweh prevents the people of the nations from accomplishing what they plan]

Here, **nations** represents either the people of the nations or the leaders of the nations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the counsel of the leaders of other nations]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **counsel**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what nations decide to do]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **plans**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what the people plan to do]

11.q: עֲצַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה לְ⁠עוֹלָ֣ם תַּעֲמֹ֑ד מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת לִ֝בּ֗⁠וֹ לְ⁠דֹ֣ר וָ⁠דֹֽר
11.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [What Yahweh has decided will endure through all generations]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **counsel**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Everything Yahweh decides]

Here the psalmist is speaking of Yahweh’s **counsel** as if it were something that could **stand** in the sense of remaining upright and stable for all time. He means that Yahweh’s decisions are permanent and will never change or fail. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [endures forever]

The psalmist is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the plans of his heart stand to generation and generation]

Here the **heart** represents where Yahweh’s thoughts and intentions exist. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [his intentions]

The psalmist is using **to generation and generation** as a common expression of his culture to mean “forever” or “through all time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [through all generations] or [forever]

12.note: The psalmist is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of joy or blessing. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Oh, how happy is the nation] or [How blessed will be the nation]

Here, **nation** represents the people of the nations. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people of the nation]

Here the psalmist is speaking of **the people** as if they were **an inheritance** that Yahweh received as a possession. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to be his own possession]

13.q: מִ֭⁠שָּׁמַיִם הִבִּ֣יט יְהוָ֑ה רָ֝אָ֗ה אֶֽת־כָּל־בְּנֵ֥י הָ⁠אָדָֽם
13.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [From the heavens, Yahweh looks down, indeed he sees all the sons of man]

The psalmist is using **the sons of man** as a common expression of the culture to mean “human beings.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [humanity] or [the people]

14.note: Here the psalmist is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a person who **gazes** from a physical **place of his dwelling**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [From where he rules, he watches carefully]

15.note: Here the **hearts** represents their inner person, including thoughts and desires. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the one forming all of their inner beings]

16.note: The expression **is not saved** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [A great army does not save the king]

The expression **is not delivered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [great strength does not deliver a warrior]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [by being very strong]

17.q: שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭⁠סּוּס לִ⁠תְשׁוּעָ֑ה וּ⁠בְ⁠רֹ֥ב חֵ֝יל֗⁠וֹ לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּֽט
17.note: See how your translation team has decided to represent pairs of phrases in Hebrew poetry that mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [The horse is a falsehood for salvation, indeed, by its great strength, it does not deliver]

Here the psalmist is speaking of the horse as if it were a lie or **a falsehood** because it gives a false sense of security. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The horse gives a false sense of security]

The psalmist is using one part of an army, a **horse**, to represent the strongest part of the army. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Having an army with strong horses]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for saving anyone]

18.note: The psalmist is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look] or [Pay attention]

Here, **the eye of Yahweh** represents Yahweh’s watchful care and attention. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the watchful attention of Yahweh]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that he will faithfully keep his covenant]

19.note: The psalmist is using **soul** to represent the people who fear Yahweh themselves from the perspective of their spiritual existence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [those who fear him]

20.note: The psalmist is using **Our soul** to represent the himself and the people from the perspective of their spiritual existence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [We ourselves wait for Yahweh]

The terms **our help** and **our shield** mean similar things. The psalmist is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [our sure protector]

Here the psalmist is speaking of Yahweh protecting his people as if he were a battle **shield**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [is our helper and our protector]

21.note: Here the **our hearts** represents their inner person, including thoughts and desires. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [we rejoice in our inner beings]

The psalmist is using the term **name** to represent who Yahweh is and his character. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in Yahweh’s holiness]

22.note: This is an imperative, but it communicates a prayer request rather than a command. The psalmist is asking Yahweh for something. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please let your covenant faithfulness, Yahweh, be upon us]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [May you be faithful to your covenant with us, Yahweh]
